name: Guyon Canal Syndrome
definition: Ulnar nerve compression at the wrist within Guyon canal, causing sensory and/or intrinsic hand motor symptoms depending on the lesion zone.

typical: Symptoms may relate to cycling or mass lesion

core: Differentiate from cubital tunnel and C8-T1 disease

investigations.principle: Electrodiagnostics help localization; ultrasound/MRI evaluates ganglion or structural causes.
investigations.MRI: Use MRI when soft-tissue, neural, marrow, occult injury, infection or other condition-specific questions require it.
investigations.radiographs: Use radiographs and/or CT according to the condition-specific imaging pathway.

amber: Space-occupying lesions or progressive motor deficit may require surgery.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Hasta/Vata-neuropathy phenotype may be documented only in parallel.

patientEducation.summary: Ulnar nerve compression at the wrist within Guyon canal, causing sensory and/or intrinsic hand motor symptoms depending on the lesion zone.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for major trauma, acute/progressive neurological deficit, severe infection/systemic illness, vascular compromise or other listed red flags.
